name: Team Voltage
missionStatement: Our mission is to empower students to explore the exciting world of Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) while fostering a lifelong journey of self-discovery. Through the values of Gracious Professionalism™ and a commitment to teamwork, innovation, and integrity, we aim to inspire and develop the next generation of ethical, enlightened leaders.

values.title: Gracious Professionalism
values.description: We compete with intensity while treating other teams, volunteers, mentors, and sponsors with respect and kindness.

values.title: Teamwork
values.description: Students from schools across Brevard County work with mentors to solve hard problems together.

values.title: Innovation
values.description: Each FIRST season gives students a new engineering challenge that rewards creative thinking, testing, and iteration.

values.title: Community Impact
values.description: We promote STEAM through FLL mentoring, the FLL Voltage Challenge, Sparky's STEAM Camp, demos, and outreach events.

history.title: Scorpsquad Roots
history.description: Team 248 “Scorpsquad” at Satellite High set the foundation for what would become Team Voltage.

history.title: County-Wide Collaboration
history.description: Students from multiple Brevard schools united to solve sponsorship challenges and formed Team Voltage 386.

history.title: Advocates for FIRST
history.description: Voltage presented to the Brevard County School Board, inspiring a district-wide push for FRC and FLL teams.

history.title: Melbourne High Home Base
history.description: The team relocated to Melbourne High School, establishing the build space we still occupy today.

history.title: FLL Host Team
history.description: We began hosting local FIRST LEGO League tournaments, mentoring dozens of younger teams.

history.title: Championship Return
history.description: After major fundraising improvements, Voltage returned to FIRST Championship in Houston.

history.title: Community Programs Expand
history.description: Sparky’s STEAM Camp and year-round outreach events now serve hundreds of students annually.

mentors.name: Juan Davila
mentors.title: Lead Mechanical Mentor
mentors.bio: Mechanical engineer at Harris/L3Harris with BS and MS degrees from Florida Tech. Juan has been part of Team Voltage since the beginning with Okie and values FIRST because it gives students a real-world challenge that changes every season.

mentors.name: DeAnn Davila
mentors.title: Controls & Inspection
mentors.bio: Manufacturing engineer at Harris/L3Harris with a BS in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Rochester. DeAnn has served FIRST for many years as a FIRST Technical Advisor, Lead Robot Inspector, and referee at regional and championship events.

mentors.name: Joe Bernier
mentors.title: Electrical Systems
mentors.bio: Retired engineering manager for Northrop Grumman and United Space Alliance at Kennedy Space Center. Joe has mentored Team Voltage since 2002, teaching students electronics, sensors, and robot controls.

mentors.name: Debbie Bernier
mentors.title: Software & Alumni Support
mentors.bio: Retired software engineer who spent 28 years developing avionics software at Rockwell Collins. Debbie joined through her children in 2002 and continues mentoring because FIRST helps students see themselves as capable college and STEM candidates.

mentors.name: Okie Baughman
mentors.title: Reliability & Fabrication
mentors.bio: Retired Harris reliability engineer with an Oklahoma State degree and Navy electronics background. Okie started with Juan on Scorp Squad in 1998 and helps students understand what engineering careers are really like.

mentors.name: Daniel Kemp
mentors.title: Operations & Alumni Mentor
mentors.bio: Supply chain professional at Harris/L3Harris. Daniel started with Team Voltage as a student in 2005, became the team's first mentor-in-training, and returned to give back to the program that taught him so much.

mentors.name: William Davies
mentors.title: Hardware & Software Integration
mentors.bio: Maritime robotics engineer at L3Harris. William began FIRST in 2006 with L.C. Bird HS Robohawks 346 and joined Voltage in 2015 after earning a BS in Aerospace Engineering, mentoring software, electrical, and mechanical integration.

mentors.name: Janielle Ziegler
mentors.title: Team Operations
mentors.bio: Project Support Specialist at Health First and Team Voltage alumna. Janielle was a student from 2007-2009, mentor-in-training from 2009-2011, returned in 2018 for Team Ops and Spirit, and became a FIRST Robotics Competition Field Supervisor in 2020.

mentors.name: Joe Foster
mentors.title: Fabrication Mentor
mentors.bio: Florida native, University of Florida mechanical engineering graduate, and FIRST coach or mentor since 2010. Joe teaches students wood construction, metal fabrication, and practical robot design skills.

mentors.name: Tom Gabeler
mentors.title: Engineering Teacher
mentors.bio: Engineering Technology teacher at Melbourne High since 2001 and FIRST mentor since 2002. Tom loves robotics and still looks forward to class every day.

faqs.question: Who can join Team Voltage?
faqs.answer: Any Brevard County high school student without an FRC team can participate—no experience required.

faqs.question: Do I need prior robotics skills?
faqs.answer: No. We teach CAD, programming, fabrication, business, and media skills with structured onboarding and mentors.

faqs.question: How much does it cost?
faqs.answer: We ask each family to support travel and fundraising, but need-based assistance is available.

faqs.question: How do sponsors help?
faqs.answer: Sponsor funding covers robot parts, event travel, community outreach, and Sparky’s STEAM Camp scholarships.
